correctedPlannerFigure.claim: The dispatch and OPS-16 P-369 say the P-340 conflict sentence's sha256 is 1ef599c6702e5d59c921f7512eca8d555e5096783a453f8ff7a9f8f940f8c051, 'the value's sha256 ... as the P-331 checker extracts it' (P-340's CP2 says the same).
correctedPlannerFigure.measured: Extracting SETBACK_SOURCE_CONFLICT_NOTE through the checker's OWN extractConst gives the sentence `Setback sources disagree on this parcel and at least one source's effective date could not be read at source — both candidates are served and neither is settled. Verify with the city.` (straight apostrophe, em dash), IDENTICAL in both repos, sha256 ef31c6abfd1a8e6fd247c701d2f2e273a0e84f732c62a2bf0864685bbb046dad.
correctedPlannerFigure.checkedNotAssumed: Brute-forced 810 variants (curly vs straight apostrophe, hyphen/en/em/horizontal-bar/minus dashes, phrase variants, quoted, trailing newline/CRLF) and scanned every doc_repo artifact and both product files for the sentence — no rendering of it hashes to 1ef599. The two whole-file sha256s P-340 also recorded ARE correct (map 44066745..., LDT 10efae66..., raw bytes).
correctedPlannerFigure.consequence: The row was landed with the TRUE value (ef31c6ab...), which is what the checker actually extracts. The `value` field is only read by --selftest fixture generation, never by the real comparison, so a wrong figure would not have broken CI — it would have shipped a close that cannot be reconciled. DEV_PROCESS 1.4 (two numbers that should agree and do not is a free finding) and 3.2a (a correction quotes the source and names the file) apply; this is recorded, not silently fixed.
